Amid massive firings, resignations, and criminal charges, Chancellor Palpatine convinces the remaining agency directors to merge their organizations into one bureau responsible for ensuring that the government remains free from internal corruption. Immediately after Emperor Palpatine reorganizes the Republic as an Empire, the agency directors unanimously agree to the provisions set forth in the New Order.

The four divisions of Imperial Intelligence are Internal Organization, the Analysis Bureau, the Bureau of Operations, and Intelligence.

In the years since, the new, unified intelligence groups again divided into separate organizations, all answering to an anonymous group of directors- the Ubiqtorate- that in turn reports directly to the Empire.
Answering directly to the Ubiqtorate, these black-ops agents act as troubleshooters for Imperial Intelligence, solving problems by the most expedient means available.
IntOrg is responsible for maintaining Imperial Intelligence's own security- protecting data and monitoring internal practices.
IntSec provides physical security, including Imperial Intelligence's force of guards and sentries.
IntCon watches Imperial Intelligence for signs of spies, saboteurs, and double agents.
Analysis sifts through all the data that is transmitted or collected within the Empire.

A great deal of the Empire's raw intelligence comes in the form of news reports. Media's job is to analyze every source of public information every day, looking for patterns or data that might otherwise be overlooked.
Signal intelligence analyzes the medium as well as the message, looking for information about the transmitter and the receiver of suspicious information.
Cryptanalysis pores over coded transmissions and applies mathematical formulas in order to decrypt them.
The Technology bureau examines non-Imperial equipment to learn how it works, then adapt it or develop countermeasures for neutralizing it.

Enemy agents captured by the Empire are delivered to Interrogation to undergo thorough questioning, using drugs, psychology, and mental and physical torture. Interrogation also sometimes uses neuroprogramming to brainwash captured agents before releasing them as double agents.
The Bureau carries out Imperial Intelligence's toughest jobs- the dirty work that requires more resources or more independent authority than other divisions can provide.
This branch of the Bureau monitors the activity of the Empire's enemies- both within and without- and is authorized to make arrests when necessary.
This branch provides highly trained double agents, spies, and sleeper agents.
Counterintelligence identifies and dismantles enemy intelligence groups working against the Empire.
DiploSer is the Empire's diplomatic corps. DiploSer's agents advice local, regional, and planetary governments on matters of trade, diplomacy, and politics.
Destab is responsible for weakening the political, cultural, commercial, and religious apparatuses of the Empire's enemies, making them more susceptible to Imperial conquest.
Agents of this division of the Bureau remove people inconvenient to the Emperor.
After Analysis has collected information, Intelligence employs an army of experts from every conceivable field of study to predict the actions of the Empire's enemies.
ExComm relays messages between various branches of Imperial Intelligence, the Ubiqtorate, and the Imperial Military.
Intelligence is composed of thousands of individual branches organized by the sector for which each is responsible.
This branch of Intelligence specifically predicts trends in the actions of groups that offer organized resistance to the Empire.

A strictly pro tem group, the Crisis branch is formed when needed, for specific purposes, from appropriate subject-matter experts. Crisis answers to the Ubiqtorate, but in rare cases it can also be placed under the command of Grand Moffs or report directly to the Emperor.
Sector Plexus ensures that the content of Imperial messages is secure, using a variety of codes, transmission protocols, and electronic encryption formats.

The basic units of Imperial Intelligence, system cells operate on every known world, carrying out instructions from the Ubiqtorate through Sector Plexus. Each cell consists of 4-20 agents. Every cell is outfitted according to its needs, but nearly all employ the RWStar A/P Transceiver, which allows agents to communicate with Sector Plexus systems.

The Imperial CompLink uses software surreptitiously installed on computers all over the Empire to monitor electronic data. This spyware transmits packets of information to Hyperspace orbiting scanners placed in strategic positions throughout the galaxy, which then relay the data to the CompLink bureau for study by Analysis. Imperial CompLink and Sector Plexus work together closely.
